title: Compass and Escarpment
premise: Casper Whitlock, a salvage diver drowning in her late father's debts, is hired to quietly recover classified equipment from a wreck the navy pretends doesn't exist. When a record-low tide exposes a sea cave beneath the escarpment, she finds a compass that points not north but toward something buried in the glacier above — and discovers the wreck, the cave, and her father's death are all threads of one secret. Pursued by the navy officer who ruined her family and by salvagers who want the compass for themselves, Casper must cross the range ahead of the snows and reach the ice-locked vault during the brief calving season when the route opens. In the end she chooses to destroy what's hidden rather than claim or sell it, paying her debt with truth instead of treasure, and finally belonging to the mountain village that took her in.
about_author: Gideon Coldharbour is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent a decade mapping coastlines from Norway to Patagonia before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people who live at the edge of maps, drawing on his own seasons aboard research vessels and in high-altitude base camps.

chapters.title: The Wreck They Don't Name
chapters.summary: Casper dives a classified wreck site off the escarpment coast, recovering a sealed case for a navy liaison who pays too well. Her POV establishes her debt, her dead father's salvage boat, and her careful invisibility. Beat: wary competence masking exhaustion.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Dead
chapters.summary: Casper tallies her father's debts against her earnings and realizes the navy contract won't cover them. A creditor's letter threatens the boat. Beat: quiet desperation hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Lowest Tide in Forty Years
chapters.summary: An old fisherman, Marta Voss, mentions a tide so low it will expose the sea cave of local legend. Casper dismisses it until she sees the waterline drop. Beat: curiosity stirring against self-preservation.

chapters.title: What the Cave Keeps
chapters.summary: Casper enters the exposed cave alone and finds a brass compass fused into rock, its needle swinging toward the glacier, not north. Navy divers arrive early; she hides. Beat: awe curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Officer Rennick
chapters.summary: Navy Lieutenant Rennick interviews Casper about 'anomalies' near the wreck; she lies smoothly but recognizes him as the officer who signed the report clearing her father's fatal last voyage. Beat: cold recognition, old grief rekindled.

chapters.title: The Needle and the Map
chapters.summary: At home Casper compares the compass to her father's charts and finds his annotations matching its bearing — he knew. She pockets the compass instead of surrendering it. Beat: inheritance as burden and invitation.

chapters.title: Buyers in the Harbor
chapters.summary: A salvage broker named Quill offers Casper a fortune for anything recovered from the cave, revealing others know it exists. She refuses badly, and now they're watching her. Beat: the trap of being noticed.

chapters.title: Marta's Story
chapters.summary: Marta tells the legend: decades ago an expedition vanished on the glacier carrying something the government wanted buried. Her brother was among them. Beat: belonging offered through shared history.

chapters.title: Raided
chapters.summary: Quill's men ransack Casper's boat searching for the compass; she escapes with it and little else, burning her old life behind her. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: The Escarpment Road
chapters.summary: Casper reaches the mountain village of Halden-at-the-Wall, gateway to the range, and trades diving skills for shelter. POV widens to include guide Eirik Solheim. Beat: first breath of belonging.

chapters.title: Eirik's Terms
chapters.summary: Eirik agrees to guide her up the glacier route but only after the calving season opens the pass — weeks away, while snows close in. Tension between waiting and pursuit. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Winter Comes Early
chapters.summary: An early storm buries the lower passes; Rennick arrives in Halden asking questions, and the village closes ranks around Casper without being asked. Beat: community as shield.

chapters.title: The Compass Lies Still
chapters.summary: Trapped indoors, Casper studies the compass: its needle steadies only when pointed at the icefall, and engraved initials match her father's. He was here. Beat: grief transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: Quill Climbs Too
chapters.summary: Word comes that Quill's crew has hired their own guide and is staging at the far side of the pass. The race is now literal. Beat: dread sharpening stakes.

chapters.title: Training on the Moraine
chapters.summary: Eirik drills Casper in crampons, crevasse rescue, and rope work; she is stronger than he expected but reckless. Beat: trust built through friction.

chapters.title: Rennick's Offer
chapters.summary: Rennick privately offers Casper full debt forgiveness if she hands over the compass and names her sources. She refuses, and understands he'll take it by force. Beat: defiance at real cost.

chapters.title: The Night Watch
chapters.summary: Someone searches Casper's room; Marta's grandson catches the intruder — one of Rennick's men. The village expels the navy party. Beat: loyalty repaid, escalation sealed.

chapters.title: Calving Season Opens
chapters.summary: Warm winds crack the glacier; the icefall shifts and opens the high route for a window of days. Eirik says they leave at dawn. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: Onto the Ice
chapters.summary: Casper, Eirik, and Marta's grandson Tomas begin the ascent. First crevasse crossing nearly kills Casper; the compass needle pulls true. Beat: terror and exhilaration entwined.

chapters.title: Camp in the Blue
chapters.summary: They shelter inside a blue-ice cave overnight; Eirik reveals his own reason for climbing — his father was on the lost expedition too. Beat: two inheritances converging.

chapters.title: The Serac Field
chapters.summary: Crossing unstable seracs, they witness a massive calving that seals the route behind them — no retreat now. Beat: commitment beyond recall.

chapters.title: Quill's Rope Team
chapters.summary: They spot Quill's team ahead, moving fast and cutting corners dangerously. A standoff at a fixed line ends in uneasy parallel travel. Beat: enemy proximity, mutual contempt.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: A whiteout separates Casper from Eirik; alone with the compass, she navigates by its impossible bearing and finds both men alive in a snow hole. Beat: the compass proves itself; faith kindles.

chapters.title: The Old Camp
chapters.summary: They discover the lost expedition's camp, bodies preserved, journals frozen open. Her father's name appears — he was the young diver who turned back. Beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: Father's Confession
chapters.summary: Reading the journal, Casper learns her father helped hide the cargo — a prototype navigation system worth fortunes — and spent his life guarding its location, dying rather than selling it. Beat: understanding replaces resentment.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Col
chapters.summary: Tomas, revealed to have been feeding information to Quill to pay his own family's debts, disables their ropes at the col. Eirik falls; Casper arrests his fall barely. Beat: betrayal and forgiveness colliding.

chapters.title: Mercy on the Ice
chapters.summary: Instead of abandoning Tomas, they rope him in — he knows the final approach. His shame becomes usefulness. Beat: mercy as strategy and grace.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath
chapters.summary: The calving season's peak opens a melt tunnel to a cavity in the glacier where the expedition cached the device, intact and glowing faintly in headlamps. Beat: wonder at the threshold.

chapters.title: Quill Arrives
chapters.summary: Quill's team storms the cavity; in the struggle the device's casing cracks and begins venting. Quill wants it whole regardless. Beat: greed versus survival.

chapters.title: Rennick on the Mountain
chapters.summary: Rennick's helicopter-borne team lands above the icefall, having tracked them all along; he orders everyone detained and the device secured for the navy. Beat: power arriving in force.

chapters.title: Three Hands on One Prize
chapters.summary: Navy, Quill, and Casper's group face each other over the leaking device as the glacier groans — the calving window is closing. Beat: standoff under a ticking sky.

chapters.title: The Glacier Decides
chapters.summary: A catastrophic calving collapses the tunnel mouth; Quill's crew flees and is lost; Rennick's team retreats upslope. Casper stays with the device. Beat: nature as arbiter.

chapters.title: What It Points To
chapters.summary: Alone with the cracked device, Casper realizes it isn't treasure but a weapon-grade guidance system her father died keeping buried. The compass was his failsafe map to destroy it. Beat: moral clarity.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Rennick returns demanding handover; Casper triggers the failsafe, collapsing the cavity and burying the device forever, the compass shattering in her hand. Beat: climax — sacrifice of fortune for principle.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Casper, Eirik, and Tomas descend the closing route through storm, roped together, half-dead, carrying only journals and bones for the families. Beat: endurance stripped to essentials.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: In Halden, Casper gives testimony; Rennick, exposed by the journals, is recalled in disgrace. Her debt is voided by court order — paid in truth. Beat: justice, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Bones Home
chapters.summary: The expedition's remains are returned; Marta buries her brother beside the sea. The village claims Casper fully, giving her father's boat a new berth. Beat: mourning and welcome braided.

chapters.title: The Empty Berth
chapters.summary: Spring: Casper refits her father's boat, deciding to stay, dive these waters, and keep the mountain's memory. Eirik asks what she'll chart next. Beat: quiet hope.

chapters.title: Compass and Escarpment
chapters.summary: Final chapter: standing on the escarpment at dawn, Casper lets the broken compass go into the tide. She belongs nowhere by accident anymore — she chose this place, and it chose her back. Beat: resolution, belonging earned.
